summary: Verified that DeepSeek V4 Pro is now the default and selectable DeepSeek model in the LLM settings provider payload, with bridge registry tests, TypeScript checks, frontend build, and Python regression tests.

results.evidence: bun test passed 3 tests, including DeepSeek V4 Pro default/selectable and legacy default normalization coverage.
bun run typecheck completed tsc --noEmit successfully.
npm --prefix frontend run typecheck completed vue-tsc --noEmit successfully.
Bun /providers probe returned status 200, default_model deepseek-v4-pro, and models [deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner].
npm --prefix frontend run build completed Vite production build successfully.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q passed 27 tests with one existing Starlette TestClient deprecation warning.

acceptance_results.evidence: Registry test and /providers probe show deepseek-v4-pro in DeepSeek models, first in the list.
Registry test and /providers probe show DeepSeek default_model as deepseek-v4-pro.

acceptance_results.requirement: Existing DeepSeek legacy defaults no longer dominate the settings panel
acceptance_results.evidence: Registry test normalizes stored deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner defaultModel values to deepseek-v4-pro for provider status.
Full Python suite, llm_bridge typecheck/test, frontend typecheck, and frontend build all passed.

coverage: Verification covers the provider status payload consumed by the LLM settings dialog, DeepSeek model chips/default_model behavior, legacy stored default normalization, TypeScript contracts on bridge/frontend, packaged frontend build, and Python web/control-plane regressions. It does not include a live DeepSeek API generation call because no user API key was provided.
manual_checks: Reviewed llm_bridge/src/registry.ts to confirm custom stored model IDs other than legacy DeepSeek defaults are preserved.
Reviewed frontend/src/types.ts to confirm ProviderStatus still exposes default_model to ProviderSettings.vue.
